summary: Lansdowne House Airport (YLH) is a small remote airfield serving the community of Lansdowne House, also known as Neskantaga, an isolated First Nations community in northern Ontario. Located along the Attawapiskat River, the airport provides a critical lifeline to the community, as there is no permanent road access and travel is largely dependent on air transport and seasonal winter roads. It primarily handles regional turboprop flights and serves as an essential link for medical evacuations, cargo, and passenger travel.
faqs:
Q: Where is Lansdowne House Airport located?
A: The airport is situated in Lansdowne House (Neskantaga First Nation), a remote community in the Kenora District of northern Ontario, Canada, along the Attawapiskat River.

Q: Is there road access to Lansdowne House?
A: No, the community has no permanent road access. Travel is by air year-round or via seasonal winter ice roads that connect to other northern communities for a limited window each year.

Q: What airlines serve Lansdowne House Airport?
A: Regional carriers such as Wasaya Airways and Nakina Air Service operate scheduled flights to the airport, typically using turboprop aircraft suited for short gravel runways.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport for passengers?
A: Facilities are minimal, consistent with a remote northern airstrip. There is no scheduled commercial terminal building comparable to larger airports, and passengers should coordinate ground transport in advance.
transport_tips: The community has no road access, so flying is essentially the only year-round option for arrival and departure. Arrange ground transportation with your host or the band office in advance, as there is no taxi or rideshare service. Cargo and passenger services should be booked well ahead, as flight schedules to remote northern Ontario can change with short notice due to weather.
local_tip: Pack all essentials including extra food, warm clothing, and any medications in your carry-on, as weather-related cancellations and delays are common and the nearest full services are hundreds of kilometres away.
